clue.text: Long odds of tango and cha-cha foes dancing together

indicators.note: the three words dance together, their letters jumbled into one new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bookmaker's view of whether two sworn enemies will ever partner each other on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing together' is the anagram signal: TANGO, CHACHA and FOES are shuffled as one pool of fifteen letters; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a very slim likelihood, much like a bet at long odds.

clue.text: '70s rock instrument used in Wales

parts.note: glam rock was the glittery, theatrical pop style of the 1970s
an organ is a keyboard instrument

explanation.surface: A keyboard from the glitter-rock era turns up in a Welsh setting.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is a historic county of south Wales, standing for part of the country rather than the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic county in the south of the principality, home to Cardiff and Swansea, so a part standing for the country.

clue.text: Perhaps put Boatman in work — a lot of it!

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: the setter's letter is placed in among the letters of the other pieces

parts.note: a ton is a lot, as in 'tons of time'
the setter, Boatman, refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: The setter invites us to slot him into a big piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' is a noun here, not a verb: in finance a put is a contract to sell, an example of the answer, flagged by 'Perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: In finance a put is a contract giving the right to sell at a set price, so it is one kind of this contract.

clue.text: Back pointless meeting: the man is after nothing? That's a record

indicators.note: the man comes after nothing, so his letters follow the zero
the meeting word loses a compass point, here S for south

parts.note: a tryst is a lovers' meeting
O looks like zero, nothing
HE is the pronoun for a man
LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A sad tale of a fruitless date, a man left with nothing, set to music on vinyl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' removes S (south, a compass point) from TRYST. 'Back' is a verb meaning support, not a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To back someone is to support them, which means making an effort to assist.

clue.text: See 10
It returns the part the Church keeps

indicators.note: the little word It turns round and is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A churchy observation that some portion always comes back to the Church.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenth of produce or income traditionally paid to support the Church and its clergy.

clue.text: French perhaps sing solver's one anthem

indicators.note: singing the phrase out loud gives a sound like another word

parts.note: solver's is 'you're' (the solver is you), one is A, and an anthem of praise is a paean: 'you're a paean'

explanation.surface: A Frenchman, say, is urged to belt out the national anthem with the solver.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'you're a paean' sounds like the answer. A paean is a hymn of praise.
explanation.definitionFit: The French are one example of the people of the continent, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Irrigation for Zimbabwe at last: an answer to prayers sent up

indicators.note: only the final letter of Zimbabwe is used
in a down clue, sending the word up reverses it

parts.note: amen is the response said at the end of a prayer

explanation.surface: Drought-stricken Zimbabwe finally gets the water it prayed for.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests farming, but the irrigation is medical: a flushing of the bowel.
explanation.definitionFit: Medically, irrigation means flushing out a body cavity, and this procedure flushes the bowel.

clue.text: Awful, stumbling hag on dance programme missing trick, you say?

indicators.note: in an across clue, the hag's letters sit on, or before, the rest
the hag stumbles, so her letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the dance show lacks the letters that follow

parts.note: Strictly Come Dancing is a BBC ballroom dance programme, known as Strictly

indicators.note: the letters removed are only spoken like the word trick, not spelt like it

parts.note: a trick, spoken aloud, gives the run T-R-I-C

explanation.surface: A clumsy old woman on a TV dance show, failing to land her trick, sounds dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes TRIC (which sounds like 'trick', hence 'you say') out of STRICTLY to leave STLY. STRICTLY is short for Strictly Come Dancing, a British TV ballroom contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean dreadful or very bad, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Creepy ghoul eats beast, exploits socially unacceptable growth promoted here

indicators.note: the scrambled ghoul takes the beast inside it
creepy suggests the ghoul's letters crawling into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
an ass is a beast of burden

indicators.note: U means upper-class, socially acceptable; making it unacceptable takes the U away

parts.note: to exploit something is to use it

explanation.surface: A horror scene in which a ghoul devours an animal, then a swipe at nasty habits flourishing somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old label for upper-class, socially acceptable usage, so 'socially unacceptable' strips it. 'growth promoted here' is plants, not bad habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants are grown under glass in these buildings, so growth is encouraged inside them.

clue.text: Harass people involved in wrongdoing

indicators.note: the people are caught up inside the wrongdoing

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men are people in the old general sense

explanation.surface: A charge of harassment against people mixed up in misconduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to persecute or torture someone persistently, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Solver taking on psychic sees, as might appear hazily, the power of subliminal suggestion

indicators.note: the letters appear hazily, blurred into a new order like a vision at a seance

parts.note: thee is an old word for you, the solver
a psychic who speaks with spirits is a medium
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A solver consulting a clairvoyant who sees things dimly, as in a vision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appear hazily' shuffles all twenty-one letters of THEE, MEDIUM, SEES, AS and MIGHT; 'taking on' only joins the solver to the psychic.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshall McLuhan's famous phrase that the way content is delivered shapes how it affects us, beneath conscious notice.

clue.text: Much to-do from zealotry at heart, on and on, using psychic powers on dead?

indicators.note: only the central letters at the heart of zealotry are used

parts.note: ESP is extrasensory perception
the late are the dead, as in 'the late king'

explanation.surface: A spiritualist's busy agenda: fanatical work, endlessly, using psychic gifts on the departed.
explanation.walkthrough: The central four letters of ZEALOTRY give ALOT; the two plain 'on's give ONON.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for having many tasks or worries to deal with, a heavy workload.

clue.text: See 10
Communicate with those we miss, who bequeath £10?

definitions.meaning: write a message for people who are out when you call

explanation.surface: A spiritual question about contacting the departed, then a joke about tiny legacies.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'note' as a banknote: a British tenner is a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing a message for someone who is absent, or literally willing a single banknote to an heir.

clue.text: After victory, reconstruct (liberate outright)

indicators.note: the rebuilt word follows the victory letter

parts.note: V is the sign and abbreviation for victory

indicators.note: to reconstruct is to rebuild the letters in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Post-war instructions: having won, rebuild, and free the place completely.
explanation.walkthrough: The parenthesis hides that 'liberate' is fodder and 'outright' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adjectives meaning thorough or complete, as in a real, absolute disaster.

clue.text: See 1
Presented headless first, it's said, for the dead came back

indicators.note: the letters for the dead come first, before the rest

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is said for the dead

indicators.note: the word loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: to host a show is to present it

explanation.surface: A ghost story: the dead returned, after a beheaded figure was put on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' points to RIP being the words said over the dead. 'came back' means replied sharply, not returned from the grave.
explanation.definitionFit: To riposte is to make a quick retort, so the past tense means answered back.

clue.text: It's not vital to get tipsy from potion

indicators.note: the letters get tipsy and reel into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Reassurance that getting a little drunk on a magic brew hardly matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both say something is unimportant, a phrase synonym for lacking significance.

clue.text: Seance appears really inexplicable at first but, as you say, it's a fabrication!

indicators.note: only the first letter of each of these four words is used

explanation.surface: A sceptic says a seance looks baffling but is all made up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabrication' looks like a lie, but here it is a thing made of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun: the Indian draped garment is literally made of fabric, rather than being a lie.

clue.text: Soaring mountain road missing from visitant's haunt

indicators.note: in a down clue, soaring means the word rises, read upwards

parts.note: an alp is a mountain

explanation.walkthrough: 'haunt' is a verb meaning trouble persistently, not a ghost's home.
explanation.definitionFit: To haunt someone is to trouble them persistently, as worries or bad luck do.

clue.text: Blame the frost? He's upset about a Xmas bloom

explanation.walkthrough: The 's of He's stands for 'is', leaving HE as fodder.

clue.text: A historic drink at pub

parts.note: ale is a drink, a type of beer

explanation.walkthrough: 'A historic' means an old form of A: the Hebrew and Phoenician letter from which A descends.

clue.text: Potions said to cause livid hue

parts.note: to bruise is to leave a purple mark on the skin

explanation.surface: A warning that some concoctions leave the drinker black and blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Mixtures made by steeping or boiling ingredients, like a witch's magic drinks.

clue.text: Morse, perhaps, out in sound and vision

indicators.note: the remaining letters are pronounced like the answer

parts.note: Morse is perhaps an inspector, the Oxford TV detective; with the word in put out, SPECTOR is left

explanation.surface: Inspector Morse turning up on radio and television.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is a British TV detective; 'out' removes IN from INSPECTOR to leave SPECTOR, and 'sound' says that is spoken like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A vision here is an apparition, a ghostly figure seen.

clue.text: Hollowly beatify dead souls? From the start, let them be

indicators.note: beatify is hollowed out, keeping only its outer letters

parts.note: gone means dead

indicators.note: only the starting letter of souls is used

explanation.surface: A plea to bless departed souls and then leave them in peace.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'let ... be ...': the past is what you agree to leave alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Past offences or grievances, which the proverb says should be forgotten and left alone.

clue.text: Phantoms from below, heralded by sulphur

explanation.walkthrough: Brimstone (sulphur) is traditionally linked with hell, so the surface hangs together.
explanation.definitionFit: Shades are ghosts or spirits of the dead in classical poetry.

clue.text: Number (one transcending 50) and one of its qualities

parts.note: e, the base of natural logarithms, is a transcendental number
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
being divisible by two, or not, is a quality of a number

explanation.surface: A mathematician's note about a number, its size and properties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transcending' is a maths pun: e is a transcendental number. 'its' refers to Number, whose qualities include being even (though this one is odd).
explanation.definitionFit: A whole number between ten and twelve, the size of a football team.
